purpose: Prototype content and peer-review preparation; not validated cultural guidance or independent evaluation data.
provenance_note: All situations, dialogue, interpretation alternatives, responses and exercises are AI-authored. Sources support only the specific background or vocabulary identified in evidence_scope. No real peer contribution or user validation is claimed.

sources.title: NUS: Singlish goes digital
sources.supports: Singlish occurs in digital messages; the article illustrates meh expressing skepticism in a particular sentence.
sources.limits: Does not validate our fictional dialogues or infer individual intent. No CoSEM records were downloaded.

sources.title: NUS: Group Work: Improving Communication, Participation and Dynamics
sources.supports: A university educator describes communication difficulties and recommends discussing differences in working styles respectfully.
sources.limits: Practice account, not evidence that all Singaporean students communicate indirectly.

sources.title: NUS Libraries: How to Give Critical Feedback Without Anyone Losing Face
sources.supports: Workshop description addresses balancing honest peer feedback with politeness and uses role play.
sources.limits: Not a validation study or dictionary of hidden meanings.

sources.title: NUS BizBeat: Office humour: Why the joke’s on you
sources.supports: Humour can be received differently and may offend regardless of intended humour.
sources.limits: Workplace discussion; our campus applications are design extrapolations, not observed findings.

sources.title: Singapore Tourism Board: Singapore Insider, Apr–Jun 2019, printed page 3
sources.supports: Glossary explains makan as food/eating, shiok as enjoyment, and bojio as referring to not being invited.
sources.limits: Vocabulary support only; does not establish the emotions or intentions in our examples. Historical glossary, not current campus validation.

sources.title: NUS: Alamak... Don’t get it? Good communication is more than grammar
sources.supports: Accessible NUS summary says language use should adapt to topic, participants and communication mode.
sources.limits: Only the accessible summary was used; the linked full commentary was not used.

cards.title: Agreement needs a referent
cards.scenario: I asked a new project teammate, "Could you help with the slides?" They replied, "Can lah." We have not discussed which slides or when.
cards.user_goal: Confirm what help is being offered.

possible_interpretations.interpretation: They are agreeing to help.
possible_interpretations.when_plausible: The reply directly answers your request.

possible_interpretations.interpretation: They are reassuring you that the task is manageable.
possible_interpretations.when_plausible: The conversation was mainly about whether the slides could be completed.

missing_context: What exactly did you ask?
Were ownership and timing already agreed?
cards.do_not_assume: Do not label the reply unreliable or reluctant because it contains lah. In this scenario, the original request lacks details.
cards.suggested_response: Thanks! Could you draft slides 3–5 by 7 pm? I will handle the introduction.

learning_check.prompt: Write a follow-up that makes this offer actionable.
success_criteria: Invites agreement instead of imposing an assumed commitment

counterexample.changed_context: The request already names slides 3–5 and 7 pm, and the teammate explicitly accepts it.
counterexample.expected_adjustment: Recognise the agreement; do not invent uncertainty solely because Singlish is used.

cards.evidence_scope: S1 supports digital Singlish generally, not a precise definition of can lah. The agreement reading is an ordinary conversational hypothesis requiring local review; S2 provides general teamwork background.

cards.title: A proposal is still under consideration
cards.scenario: I suggested using interviews for our project. A teammate said, "Can consider." The meeting moved on without assigning anyone to interview participants.
cards.user_goal: Find out whether the team has chosen the method.

possible_interpretations.interpretation: The idea remains an option.
possible_interpretations.when_plausible: Alternatives are still being discussed.

possible_interpretations.interpretation: The teammate is hesitant or wants more information.
possible_interpretations.when_plausible: They have concerns that have not yet been explained.

missing_context: Did anyone explicitly approve the method?
What options or constraints are still open?
cards.do_not_assume: Do not translate this automatically as a hidden no, or as permission to start collecting data.
cards.suggested_response: Would you like us to compare interviews with the other options before deciding?

learning_check.prompt: Ask for a decision without accusing the teammate of rejecting you.

counterexample.changed_context: The teammate adds, "Yes, let’s use interviews; I will draft the questions."
counterexample.expected_adjustment: Acknowledge that the later statement resolves the earlier ambiguity.

cards.evidence_scope: General teamwork and context-sensitive communication principles only; the exact phrase and interpretations are synthetic and not established Singapore-specific meanings.

cards.title: A question may express surprise
cards.scenario: I remind the group that the report is due tonight. A teammate writes, "Need to submit tonight meh?" I worry that they are challenging me.
cards.user_goal: Clarify the deadline without escalating disagreement.

possible_interpretations.interpretation: They doubt that tonight is the deadline.
possible_interpretations.when_plausible: They remember a different date.

possible_interpretations.interpretation: They are surprised and asking for confirmation.
possible_interpretations.when_plausible: They have just learned about the deadline.

missing_context: What does the assignment page say?
Is this the final deadline or a team draft deadline?
cards.do_not_assume: Do not infer hostility from meh or treat the teammate’s doubt as evidence that the deadline changed.
cards.suggested_response: Let’s check the assignment page together. Are we talking about the final submission or our team’s draft deadline?

learning_check.prompt: If the official deadline is actually tonight, how would you change the response?

counterexample.changed_context: The assignment page says Friday and no earlier team deadline was agreed.
counterexample.expected_adjustment: Correct your reminder rather than defending an unsupported deadline.

cards.evidence_scope: The NUS example supports a skeptical use of meh; the deadline scenario and reply are original hypothetical applications.

cards.title: An invitation may use an unfamiliar word
cards.scenario: A classmate I have just met asks, "Want to makan after class?" I do not know whether this is a study session or a social invitation.
cards.user_goal: Understand the activity and decide whether to join.

possible_interpretations.interpretation: They are inviting you to eat.
possible_interpretations.when_plausible: Makan refers to food or eating in this usage.

possible_interpretations.interpretation: The meal may also include project talk.
possible_interpretations.when_plausible: They mention the project or bring the group along; the word alone does not tell you this.

missing_context: Where and when are they going?
Is there anything you need to ask about food options?
cards.do_not_assume: Do not assume the invitation means they will pay or that attendance is required.
cards.suggested_response: Thanks, I’d like to join. Where are you planning to eat?

learning_check.prompt: Decline warmly while leaving room for another invitation.
success_criteria: Does not promise attendance you cannot manage

counterexample.changed_context: They say, "We need to finish the project discussion over lunch."
counterexample.expected_adjustment: Recognise the stated work purpose and clarify an alternative if you cannot attend.

cards.evidence_scope: Makan’s food/eating meaning is sourced; the invitation, payment caution and learning task are authored examples.

cards.title: A playful complaint can also be a real request
cards.scenario: I mention getting lunch with two classmates. Another classmate replies, "Bojio!" I am unsure whether they are joking or upset.
cards.user_goal: Acknowledge the remark without guessing their feelings.

possible_interpretations.interpretation: They may be playfully saying they were not invited.
possible_interpretations.when_plausible: The exchange is relaxed and this style of joking is familiar between you.

possible_interpretations.interpretation: They may actually want to be included.
possible_interpretations.when_plausible: They say they felt left out or this has happened repeatedly.

missing_context: Have they previously asked to join?
What else did they say?
cards.do_not_assume: Do not dismiss the remark as definitely a joke or conclude they are angry from the word alone.
cards.suggested_response: It was a last-minute lunch. Would you like me to message you next time?

learning_check.prompt: What would you change if they said they had felt excluded several times?
success_criteria: Offers a practical inclusion step without demanding they laugh

counterexample.changed_context: They explicitly say, "I felt left out, and I’m not joking."
counterexample.expected_adjustment: Take that explanation seriously; do not override it with a glossary.

cards.evidence_scope: Bojio’s invitation-related meaning is sourced. Playfulness versus disappointment is a hypothetical distinction, not a documented account of this interaction.

cards.title: An enthusiastic word can be used ironically
cards.scenario: After an extra early meeting is announced, a teammate posts, "Another 8 am meeting. Shiok." There are no other messages explaining how they feel.
cards.user_goal: Check whether the meeting time works.

possible_interpretations.interpretation: They may genuinely like the arrangement.
possible_interpretations.when_plausible: They prefer early meetings or explicitly say the time suits them.

possible_interpretations.interpretation: They may be using positive wording ironically.
possible_interpretations.when_plausible: An unwanted extra meeting is being framed as enjoyable.

missing_context: Have they stated a scheduling preference?
Was this a reply to a complaint or a positive comment?
cards.do_not_assume: Do not infer sarcasm from the word alone, or infer tone of voice from text.
cards.suggested_response: Does 8 am work for you, or should we look for another time?

learning_check.prompt: Ask a scheduling question that works whether the remark is sincere or ironic.
success_criteria: Does not claim to know the emotion

counterexample.changed_context: They add, "I prefer mornings, so this is perfect."
counterexample.expected_adjustment: Use the explicit preference and interpret the message as positive.

cards.evidence_scope: Shiok’s positive meaning is sourced; the ironic usage in this invented sentence is an author hypothesis awaiting review.

cards.title: Exaggerated praise after a mistake
cards.scenario: I arrive ten minutes late to a project meeting. A teammate says, "Excellent timing!" and laughs. I do not know whether to laugh back.
cards.user_goal: Respond to the lateness and clarify expectations.

possible_interpretations.interpretation: It may be teasing about arriving late.
possible_interpretations.when_plausible: The positive wording contrasts with the late arrival.

possible_interpretations.interpretation: It may express actual frustration through humour.
possible_interpretations.when_plausible: Others have been waiting or lateness is recurring.

missing_context: Had the meeting started?
Were they genuinely waiting for something you brought?
cards.do_not_assume: Do not label the person hostile or tell the user to accept teasing. This is not uniquely Singaporean language.
cards.suggested_response: Sorry I’m late. What did I miss? I’ll let you know earlier if I’m delayed next time.

learning_check.prompt: Write a reply that addresses your lateness without guessing their intent.

counterexample.changed_context: You arrive exactly as the group needs your adapter and they say so.
counterexample.expected_adjustment: Recognise that the praise can be literal.

cards.evidence_scope: General humour background only. The phrase, scenario, interpretations and response are original, not source quotations or local usage findings.

cards.title: A joke does not remove your right to set a boundary
cards.scenario: A classmate imitates my accent while retelling something I said. I tell them I dislike it. They reply, "Just joking."
cards.user_goal: Set a clear boundary without having to prove their intent.

possible_interpretations.interpretation: They may have intended humour.
possible_interpretations.when_plausible: They describe it as a joke; that describes their account of intent, not its impact.

possible_interpretations.interpretation: They may be minimising your objection.
possible_interpretations.when_plausible: They continue after you ask them to stop.

missing_context: Do you feel comfortable replying directly?
Did the behaviour stop after your request?
cards.do_not_assume: Do not call accent imitation a Singaporean norm or require the user to tolerate it to fit in.
cards.suggested_response: I understand you meant it as a joke, but I don’t like my accent being imitated. Please stop.

learning_check.prompt: Write a boundary that names the behaviour and the change you want.

counterexample.expected_adjustment: Acknowledge the changed behaviour; do not assert an ongoing pattern without evidence.

cards.evidence_scope: General distinction between intended humour and reception; campus boundary response is an author recommendation, not an institutional policy. If it persists, the user can choose a trusted campus support contact.

cards.title: A mild suggestion can still be actionable
cards.expression_or_event: Maybe we could shorten the introduction a little.
cards.scenario: During rehearsal, a teammate says, "Maybe we could shorten the introduction a little." Our presentation is two minutes over the limit.
cards.user_goal: Turn feedback into a specific edit.

possible_interpretations.interpretation: They are suggesting a real reduction in length.
possible_interpretations.when_plausible: The rehearsal is over time.

possible_interpretations.interpretation: They are inviting discussion about where to cut.
possible_interpretations.when_plausible: They phrase the suggestion collaboratively rather than specifying an edit.

missing_context: How much time must be removed?
Which content is essential?
cards.do_not_assume: Do not dismiss the suggestion because it uses maybe, or infer that they dislike your work overall.
cards.suggested_response: Would cutting the background example help? Let’s aim for a one-minute introduction.

learning_check.prompt: Ask for one concrete editing priority.
success_criteria: Links the change to the time limit

counterexample.changed_context: The presentation is within the limit and they say shortening is optional.
counterexample.expected_adjustment: Treat it as an optional proposal rather than an urgent requirement.

cards.evidence_scope: General constructive-feedback background only; this English sentence is not a fixed Singaporean code.

cards.title: An observation may point to a work problem
cards.scenario: A teammate reviews my slides and says, "This slide is quite text-heavy." They do not suggest an edit.
cards.user_goal: Understand the concern and choose a useful revision.

possible_interpretations.interpretation: They may find the slide difficult to scan.
possible_interpretations.when_plausible: There are several long paragraphs.

possible_interpretations.interpretation: They may simply be describing its format.
possible_interpretations.when_plausible: The slide is an appendix intended for detailed reading.

missing_context: Is it a live presentation slide or a reading handout?
Which part is hard to follow?
cards.do_not_assume: Do not translate quite into a fixed level of criticism or assume the person is judging your ability.
cards.suggested_response: Which part is hardest to scan? I can move the detail into notes and keep three main points.

learning_check.prompt: How would your edit differ for a reading handout?
success_criteria: Adapts to the purpose of the document

counterexample.changed_context: It is a reference handout and the reviewer says the detail is useful.
counterexample.expected_adjustment: Do not remove needed detail merely to follow the original card.

cards.evidence_scope: General feedback and context adaptation only. The exact interpretations and edits are authored hypotheses.

cards.title: Silence is not a recorded decision
cards.expression_or_event: No replies after “Is everyone okay with this plan?”
cards.scenario: I post a project plan in a new group chat and ask if everyone agrees. Nobody replies for two hours. I wonder whether they are politely rejecting it.
cards.user_goal: Get an explicit decision before depending on the plan.

possible_interpretations.interpretation: People may not have read or considered it yet.
possible_interpretations.when_plausible: Their availability is unknown.

possible_interpretations.interpretation: Some may have concerns or think no reply is needed.
possible_interpretations.when_plausible: The group has no agreed response convention.

missing_context: What response time has the group agreed?
How soon is the decision needed?
cards.do_not_assume: Do not interpret silence as agreement, rejection, or a national communication trait.
cards.suggested_response: Could everyone confirm or suggest changes by 6 pm? We need to choose a plan before dividing the tasks.

learning_check.prompt: Write a follow-up that sets a response time without blaming anyone.

counterexample.changed_context: Everyone already explicitly approved the same plan in the meeting.
counterexample.expected_adjustment: Recognise that prior approval; ask only about any new changes.

cards.evidence_scope: General group communication background; no source claim establishes what a two-hour silence means.

cards.title: Direct disagreement can be task-focused
cards.expression_or_event: This claim is not supported by our data.
cards.scenario: A teammate comments on my draft, "This claim is not supported by our data." They highlight a sentence but add no greeting or praise.
cards.user_goal: Check the substance of the feedback and respond constructively.

possible_interpretations.interpretation: They are identifying a specific evidence problem.
possible_interpretations.when_plausible: They point to a claim that may exceed the results.

possible_interpretations.interpretation: You may be using different interpretations of the evidence.
possible_interpretations.when_plausible: You can identify relevant data that they may have missed.

missing_context: Which evidence supports the claim?
What wording would accurately reflect the result?
cards.do_not_assume: Do not infer dislike or rudeness solely from direct wording. Direct feedback can occur in any group.
cards.suggested_response: Thanks for flagging it. Which part goes beyond the data? I can revise the wording or point to the supporting result.

learning_check.prompt: Respond if you believe the claim is supported.
success_criteria: Keeps disagreement focused on the claim

counterexample.changed_context: The teammate adds a personal insult unrelated to the draft.
counterexample.expected_adjustment: Separate the valid evidence question from the inappropriate personal remark; do not excuse the insult as direct feedback.

cards.evidence_scope: General constructive-feedback background; the scenario is deliberately direct to counter a blanket indirectness stereotype.
